title: Caloric cooling devices and systems - Nature Energy
text:
AbstractCaloric cooling technologies, including magnetocaloric, elastocaloric, electrocaloric and barocaloric effects, are emerging as solid-state alternatives to conventional refrigeration, with the potential to eliminate high-global-warming-potential refrigerants. However, translating these material-level effects into efficient and scalable cooling systems remains a major challenge. Here we review the development of caloric cooling devices and systems, focusing on performance, scalability and prospects for practical deployment. We benchmark key performance metrics, including efficiency, temperature span, cooling power density, durability and cost, against vapour-compression and thermoelectric technologies. Despite large caloric effects, a gap persists between intrinsic material performance and device-level operation. Recent advances, including fatigue-resistant shape memory alloys, multilayer electrocaloric architectures and natural rubber-based elastocaloric systems, have improved durability, power density and cost-effectiveness. We further analyse system integration and cost trends and outline a roadmap to accelerate the transition towards sustainable cooling technologies.
